valuation_philosophy.model_type: AFFO-capitalization / cost-of-equity model (REIT), NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Argosy is a levered NZX diversified REIT. Reported NPAT swings on unrealised fair-value revaluations (FY2021 +$241.7m, FY2023 -$80.8m) and is not a cash-flow proxy. Reported operating cash flow minus capex is distorted by development capex and negative in several years. The owner-earnings base used here is company-disclosed AFFO (Adjusted Funds From Operations), which already deducts maintenance capex and leasing incentives and approximates sustainable equity-level distributable cash flow. Because AFFO is measured after interest expense, it is discounted at the REIT's cost of equity (not WACC), and net debt is NOT subtracted a second time from the resulting equity value -- doing so would double-count the leverage already embedded in AFFO. Terminal value is capitalized using an exit AFFO yield (P/AFFO multiple) consistent with the stock's 10-year trading range of roughly 13-24x AFFO/share (NZ$0.90-1.65 price range). The valuation is cross-checked against two bounds: (1) a no-growth AFFO-capitalization floor (current AFFO/share / cost of equity, in perpetuity) and (2) NTA/share ($1.60 FY2026) as a ceiling proxy for replacement/liquidation value. The base-case intrinsic value of $0.89 sits between the $0.71 AFFO-capitalization floor and the $1.60 NTA ceiling, as expected for a REIT trading at a persistent discount to book (current P/NTA 0.65x).

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual Report FY2026 FFO/AFFO reconciliation note; SBC negligible (<$0.3m/yr) but deducted per policy
inputs.dilution_source: DRP (dividend reinvestment plan); no buybacks; historical share count CAGR FY2022-26 ~0.79%/yr, DRP suspended for Q4 FY2026 dividend following divestment proceeds but modelled at long-run 1%/yr

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management-guided qualitative build: 9.3% under-renting reversion (3.5% annualised FY2026 rent-review uplift) partially offset by higher average interest cost as green bonds refinance; AFFO has been range-bound $48-60m for 7 years with no clear compounding trend, so base case uses low-single-digit growth rather than extrapolating a raw historical CAGR
historical_growth.notes: Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGR selection logic does NOT apply to this REIT. NPAT and equity book value are dominated by unrealised fair-value swings (equity fell from $1,472m FY2022 to $1,224m FY2024 purely on cap-rate-driven revaluation losses, then recovered to $1,398m FY2026) and are explicitly excluded as growth drivers per the AFFO-based model. AFFO 5yr CAGR is negative only because FY2021 was an unusually strong base year (post-COVID low-rate refinancing); the FY2023-26 3yr CAGR of 0.6% and revenue CAGR of ~2.7-4.0% better represent the underlying trend and support the 1.8% base-case assumption.

base.notes: Rent reversion capture continues at a moderate pace; interest costs stabilise as green bonds refinance at current OCR (2.25%); no NTA discount closure assumed; exit yield roughly matches the stock's current trading yield

bull.notes: Rate-cut tailwind accelerates interest expense relief; fuller reversion capture on the 9.3% under-rented book; green industrial development pipeline lifts industrial weighting toward 60-70% target; partial closure of NTA discount as cap rates compress further

bear.notes: Wellington office/government-tenant stress (space consolidation, fiscal restraint) offsets industrial reversion gains; higher-for-longer rate environment as some banks now forecast OCR back toward ~3% into 2027, pressuring refinancing costs on ARG020/ARG030 green bond maturities; AFFO held flat

base.note: No net-debt deduction: AFFO is already an equity-level, post-interest cash flow, so subtracting net debt again would double-count leverage

cross_checks.affo_capitalization_floor_basis: Current AFFO/share (6.734 cps) capitalized in perpetuity at base-case cost of equity (9.5%), zero growth -- represents a floor value assuming no reversion capture or development upside whatsoever
cross_checks.nta_ceiling_basis: FY2026 book NTA/share -- proxy for replacement/liquidation value; REIT has traded at a persistent discount to NTA since FY2023 (currently 0.65x)

base.note: No net-debt deduction here either, for the same reason as the intrinsic value calc (AFFO is post-interest). TV_5 is computed using the base-case exit yield (7%, i.e. the fair-value assumption a buyer pays at exit) but discounted back to today at the 15% hurdle rate, not the cost of equity.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = cost of equity (7.5%-11.5%), Columns = exit AFFO yield (5.0%-9.0%); base-case AFFO growth (1.8%) held constant

warnings: This is a REIT AFFO-capitalization model, not a standard owner-FCF DCF -- reported NPAT and equity book value are unsuitable growth drivers due to unrealised fair-value revaluation swings
Occupancy has declined from 99.3% (FY2023) to 94.6% (FY2026) and WALT has shortened from 6.1yrs to 5.0yrs -- a continuation of this trend would pressure AFFO growth below even the bear case

Two green bond maturities (ARG020 $100m Oct-2026 already repaid via refinanced $725m facility; ARG030 $125m Oct-2027) create refinancing-rate sensitivity not separately modelled beyond the cost-of-equity/exit-yield scenarios
Terminal value is 67-75% of equity value across scenarios -- typical for a REIT capitalization model but means the valuation is highly sensitive to the exit yield assumption (see sensitivity matrix)

sanity_check.note: REIT model: earnings multiples use AFFO (company-disclosed, SBC-adjusted), not GAAP EPS, because reported NPAT swings on unrealised fair-value revaluations (FY2021 +$241.7m, FY2023 -$80.8m). These will not match published P/E figures on Yahoo/screeners. P/B uses reported equity (NTA-backed). EV/EBITDA unavailable: fair-value model, no P&L D&A, no clean EBITDA disclosure.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.p_affo_note: FY2020-FY2026 FY-end closes vs SBC-adjusted AFFO; FY2022 (24.3x, ultra-low-rate era) treated as outlier and excluded from avg (incl. it: 17.7x)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/AFFO 13.28x is 0.80x the ex-outlier historical average (16.6x) and implied P/B 0.559x is below both the 10yr average (0.811x) and the current 0.653x. Base-case upside is negative (-14.4%), so the peak-extrapolation / >100%-upside checks cannot trip. The model is conservative relative to history by construction: AFFO base is mid-range of a flat 7yr series, growth 1.8% vs 2.7% revenue CAGR, and TV uses a 14.3x exit P/AFFO within the historical 13-24x range.
